text.p: McDonald's Corp said Thursday that it expects 1997 to be another record-breaking year.

Earlier, it reported earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.58 a share after a $48.7 million after-tax charge, up from $0.51 a year ago. For the year, it earned $2.21 a share after charges, up from $1.97 a year ago.

In a statement, Michael Quinlan, chairman, said 1996 results were achieved despite the intensely competitive U.S. environment, weak economies in several major international markets, severe weather, weaker foreign currencies and difficult comparisons with strong performances in many markets in 1995.
"We are confident in our growth strategies and expect 1997 to be another record-breaking year," Quinlan added.
The fast-food giant, which has more than 21,000 restaurants, said its U.S. operations did not meet the company's performance goal in 1996.

"McDonald's standards for performance remain high, and we were not satisfied with U.S. operating performance in 1996, which fell short of our goals in a highly competitive, changing consumer environment," Jack Greenberg, company vice chairman and chairman-U.S.A., said in a statement.
He added the focus in 1997 will be on boosting sales at existing restaurants with improvements in marketing, service and its menu.
McDonald's said its operating income in the United States fell 28 percent to $217.7 million in the fourth quarter. Sales in the quarter rose three percent due to restaurant expansion.
For the year, McDonald's U.S. sales rose three percent and its operating income fell nine percent.
McDonald's said its U.S. same-store sales -- measuring results from units open at least a year -- were negative in both the fourth quarter and the year.
Outside the United States, McDonald's sales rose 11 percent in the fourth quarter due mostly to restaurant expansion, and operating income gained 14 percent.
If foreign exchange rates had remained at 1995 levels, sales outside the United States would have increased at 15 percent for the fourth quarter and the year, it added.
For the year, both sales and operating income outside the United States rose 10 percent.

Excluding the impact of weaker foreign currencies and a $16 million charge related to Mexican restaurant sites, operating income outside the United States increased 14 percent for the year and 17 percent for the quarter, it added.
